data.title: UBS: Silver Has Fallen Nearly 70% From Its High and Could Rebound More Than Gold
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, UBS Global Wealth Management Chief Investment Office strategist Dominic Schnider said in a report on November 27 that silver was oversold after a major sell-off and had medium-term investment value. UBS expects silver to rebound more than gold next year.

Silver has fallen nearly 70% from its high this year. UBS said the speed and scale of the decline were comparable only to sell-offs during the global financial crisis and the early 1980s. It said silver had fallen too far for a 12-month investment horizon, while the gold-to-silver ratio had risen to 88, indicating some relative valuation appeal for silver but not extreme undervaluation.

UBS sees silver supply and demand as more balanced, with a slight tilt toward surplus. That differs from the Silver Institute’s forecast of a 35 million-ounce global supply deficit in 2026. This quarter, net noncommercial silver futures positions fell by about 36 million ounces, while silver ETFs recorded net inflows of nearly 14 million ounces.

UBS expects the Federal Reserve’s rate-hiking cycle to end in the first quarter of 2027 and U.S. inflation to decline more clearly from the second quarter. It said those shifts could revive expectations of Fed rate cuts and investment demand for precious metals. UBS favors holding long silver positions in the coming months. With short-term implied volatility on silver options near 50%, it said investors could consider selling put options for additional income, while taking on the risk of further price declines.

data.title: Bittensor Raises Subnet Limit to 160; @const_reborn Sees Potential for 512 or More
data.description: Bittensor has raised its subnet limit to 160, and @const_reborn said it could eventually reach 512 or more. According to Odaily, the OpenTensor Foundation said on X that the increase lowers registration costs and gives smaller teams more time to build and demonstrate their capabilities, as discussed by Const in the latest episode of Novelty Search. Const, @markjeffrey and @mogmachine also discussed using Gamma to bring Bittensor’s AI services to users outside the network and plans for permissionless lending to increase subnet liquidity.

data.title: Conferences Are Becoming Newsrooms as Coverage Extends Beyond Events
data.description: Conferences are increasingly functioning as newsrooms, with their value extending beyond attendance to the coverage and content they generate. BeInCrypto’s TOKEN2049 Singapore coverage reached readers after the event ended, according to BeInCrypto, with 49% of article readership coming afterward and 46% reading in a language other than English. Over two days in October 2026, its NewsDesk recorded 24 interviews that became 56 videos, clips and newsletter features; coverage totaled 117 pieces across 26 language editions and other channels, with potential reach exceeding 8.8 million. The article announcing The State of AI Agent Payments 2026 received 83% of its views after the event. More broadly, 54% of commercial publishers surveyed by the Reuters Institute in 2026 identified online and in-person events as an important revenue stream. The article also points to AI discovery as a reason event coverage can have a longer life: Muck Rack found earned media accounted for about 84% of links cited by AI assistants. Organizers and publishers still face cost pressures and difficulty measuring return on investment.

data.title: LlamaRisk Proposes Lower Aave V3 Supply and Borrowing Caps for WBTC and LINK, Plus USDC Rate Model Changes
data.description: LlamaRisk proposed lowering supply and borrowing caps for several assets on Aave V3 and changing the USDC interest-rate model. According to Foresight News, the Aave risk service provider based its recommendations on user behavior, on-chain liquidity and position health. In the Core market, it proposed reducing WBTC’s supply cap from 41,000 to 39,000 tokens and LINK’s from 8 million to 7.6 million tokens, while lowering LINK’s borrowing cap from 500,000 to 300,000 tokens. It also recommended reducing USDC’s optimal usage ratio from 91% to 90%. In the Mantle market, LlamaRisk proposed cutting USDe’s supply cap from 25 million to 10 million tokens and its borrowing cap from 10 million to 5 million tokens. At USDC’s current utilization rate of 79.3%, the adjustment would increase its floating annual borrowing rate from 4.22% to 4.26%. The changes would be implemented through the Risk Steward process.

data.title: UK FCA Proposes DeFi Access Limits for Regulated Exchanges and Platform Rules for Tokenized Stocks
data.description: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) is proposing rules that would require DeFi service providers to obtain authorization and prohibit regulated exchanges from directing retail customers to decentralized markets. According to Odaily, trading in tokenized stocks would also have to take place on regulated platforms; the proposals have not yet taken effect.
